What's a spicule?

What it isTiny CICA spicules in a watery serum. Smaller than a grain of sand.
Why bumpsClosed comedones are dead skin and oil stuck right under the surface.The spicules exfoliate the top layer as you tap, so the bumps flatten out.

How to shoot it

Talking points, not a script. Say it how you'd actually say it.
1Open on your bumps
  • Shoot your bumps like this clip. Forehead, chin or cheek, phone almost touching your skin, hard side light so every bump throws a shadow. No filter, no product. This is the hook, so it has to be obvious.
  • ⭐ Text: closed comedones?
"if your chin looks like this, it's not acne. it's closed comedones"
2Same spot, after
  • Hard cut to the same spot, smooth. Same side light, fingertip across it. Makeup back on if you want, it should sit flat now.
  • ⭐ Text: this is skin texture with spicule
"and this is the same spot now. no filter. here's what did it"
3Green screen the clipOptional
  • Green screen effect: the viral Korean pharmacist clip full screen, you in the bottom corner. Let it play 3 to 5 seconds while you react. Pick one of the 3 below, or skip this step.
  • ⭐ Text: the OG Korean spicule
"and Korea already went viral fixing them. this is the OG Korean spicule, the one everyone's been copying"
4Tap on the original
  • Tap the serum over the bumps. No rubbing. Bottle in the shot. Keep the wince.
  • ⭐ Text: tap. don't rub.
"it's a Korean spicule serum. you tap it in, you don't rub it in""it tingles a lil. that's literally the spicules doing their thing. save this if your bumps never go away"
